arxiv-2009-09677.title: CURIE: A Cellular Automaton for Concept Drift Detection
arxiv-2009-09677.creator: Jesus L. Lobo, Javier Del Ser, Eneko Osaba, Albert Bifet, Francisco Herrera
arxiv-2009-09677.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Jesus L. Lobo, Javier Del Ser, Eneko Osaba, Albert Bifet, Francisco Herrera. Data stream mining extracts information from large quantities of data flowing fast and continuously (data streams). They are usually affected by changes in the data distribution, giving rise to a phenomenon referred to as concept drift . Thus, learning models must detect and adapt to such changes, so as to exhibit a good predictive performance after a drift has occurred.

arxiv-2102-05604.title: Scalable multicomponent spectral analysis for high-throughput data annotation
arxiv-2102-05604.creator: R. Patrick Xian, Ralph Ernstorfer, Philipp M. Pelz
arxiv-2102-05604.description: Abstract Orchestrating parametric fitting of multicomponent spectra at scale is an essential yet underappreciated task in high-throughput quantification of materials and chemical composition. To automate the annotation process for spectroscopic and diffraction data collected in counts of hundreds to thousands, we present a systematic approach compatible with high-performance computing infrastructures using the MapReduce model and task-based parallelization.

arxiv-2107-10096.title: Vibrational resonance amplification in a thermo-optic optomechanical nanocavity
arxiv-2107-10096.creator: Guilhem Madiot, Sylvain Barbay, Rémy Braive
arxiv-2107-10096.description: Abstract Vibrational resonance amplifies a weak low-frequency signal by use of an additional non-resonant high-frequency modulation. The realization of weak signal enhancement in integrated nonlinear optical nanocavities is of great interest for nanophotonic applications where optical signals may be of low power.

arxiv-2107-11600.title: Noether Currents and Maxwell-type Equations of Motion in Higher Derivative Gravity Theories
arxiv-2107-11600.creator: Taichiro Kugo Yukawa Institute for Theoretical Physics, Kyoto University, Kyoto 606-8502, Japan
arxiv-2107-11600.description: Abstract In general coordinate invariant gravity theories whose Lagrangians contain arbitrarily high order derivative fields, the Noether currents for the global translation and for the Nakanishi’s O ​ S ​ p ​ ( 8 | 8 ) {O\kern-1.1ptS\kern-0.39993ptp}(8|8) choral symmetry containing the BRS symmetry as its member, are constructed.

arxiv-2301-10841.title: Free Join : Unifying Worst-Case Optimal and Traditional Joins CCS: Information systems Join algorithms
arxiv-2301-10841.creator: Yisu Remy Wang, Max Willsey, Dan Suciu
arxiv-2301-10841.description: Abstract . Over the last decade, worst-case optimal join ( WCOJ ) algorithms have emerged as a new paradigm for one of the most fundamental challenges in query processing: computing joins efficiently. Such an algorithm can be asymptotically faster than traditional binary joins, all the while remaining simple to understand and implement.

arxiv-2405-01167.title: Ergodic Spectral Efficiency Analysis of Intelligent Omni-Surface Aided Systems Suffering From Imperfect CSI and Hardware Impairments Thanks: L. Hanzo would like to acknowledge the financial support of the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council projects EP/W016605/1, EP/X01228X/1, EP/Y026
arxiv-2405-01167.creator: Qingchao Li, Graduate Student Member, IEEE, Mohammed El-Hajjar, Senior Member, IEEE
arxiv-2405-01167.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Qingchao Li, Graduate Student Member, IEEE, Mohammed El-Hajjar, Senior Member, IEEE. In contrast to the conventional reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS), intelligent omni-surfaces (IOS) are capable of full-space coverage of smart radio environments by simultaneously transmitting and reflecting the incident signals. In this paper, we investigate the ergodic spectral efficiency of IOS-aided systems for transmission over random channel links, while considering both realistic imperfect channel state information (CSI) and transceiver hardware impairments (HWIs).

arxiv-2405-09053.title: Deep Learning-Based CSI Feedback for XL-MIMO Systems in the Near-Field Domain
arxiv-2405-09053.creator: Zhangjie Peng, Ruijing Liu, Zhaotian Li, Cunhua Pan, Jiangzhou Wang
arxiv-2405-09053.description: Abstract In this paper, we consider an extremely large-scale massive multiple-input-multiple-output (XL-MIMO) system. As the scale of antenna arrays increases, the range of near-field communications also expands. In this case, the signals no longer exhibit planar wave characteristics but spherical wave characteristics in the near-field channel, which makes the channel state information (CSI) highly complex.

arxiv-2405-16978.title: OSLO: One-Shot Label-Only Membership Inference Attacks
arxiv-2405-16978.creator: Yuefeng Peng, Jaechul Roh, Subhransu Maji, Amir Houmansadr
arxiv-2405-16978.description: Abstract We introduce One-Shot Label-Only (OSLO) membership inference attacks (MIAs), which accurately infer a given sample’s membership in a target model’s training set with high precision using just a single query , where the target model only returns the predicted hard label.

arxiv-2502-13539.title: Bursting Filter Bubble: Enhancing Serendipity Recommendations with Aligned Large Language Models
arxiv-2502-13539.creator: Yunjia Xi 1∗† , Muyan Weng 1∗† , Wen Chen 2‡ , Chao Yi 2 , Dian Chen 2 , Gaoyang Guo 2 , Mao Zhang 2 , Jian Wu 2 , Yuning Jiang 2 , Qingwen Liu 2 , Yong Yu 1 , Weinan Zhang 1‡
arxiv-2502-13539.description: Abstract . Recommender systems (RSs) often suffer from the feedback loop phenomenon, i.e. , RSs are trained on data biased by their recommendations. This leads to the filter bubble effect that reinforces homogeneous content and reduces user satisfaction. To this end, serendipity recommendations, which offer unexpected yet relevant items, are proposed.

arxiv-2506-06623.title: Neural Operators for Forward and Inverse Potential–Density Mappings in Classical Density Functional Theory
arxiv-2506-06623.creator: Runtong Pan, Xinyi Fang, Kamyar Azizzadenesheli, Miguel Liu-Schiaffini, Mengyang Gu, Jianzhong Wu ∗
arxiv-2506-06623.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Runtong Pan, Xinyi Fang, Kamyar Azizzadenesheli, Miguel Liu-Schiaffini, Mengyang Gu, Jianzhong Wu ∗. Neural operators are capable of capturing nonlinear mappings between infinite-dimensional functional spaces, offering a data-driven approach to modeling complex functional relationships in classical density functional theory (cDFT).

arxiv-2511-05495.title: IMDMR: An Intelligent Multi-Dimensional Memory Retrieval System for Enhanced Conversational AI
arxiv-2511-05495.creator: Tejas Pawar 1 Dr. Sarika Patil 2 Om Tilekar 3 University of Delaware Dr. Vishwanath Karad MIT-World University of Delaware Delaware, USA Pune, Maharashtra, India Delaware,USA tejasp@udel.edu sarika.patil@mitwpu.edu.in otilekar@udel.edu Rushikesh Janwade 4 Vaibhav Helambe 5 IIT Bhubaneswar IIT Palakk
arxiv-2511-05495.description: Abstract Conversational AI systems often struggle with maintaining coherent, contextual memory across extended interactions, limiting their ability to provide personalized and contextually relevant responses. This paper presents IMDMR (Intelligent Multi-Dimensional Memory Retrieval), a novel system that addresses these limitations through a multi-dimensional search architecture.

pmc-10570442.creator: Nan Zheng, Longfu Jiang, Jiabo Shen, Jinyan Zhong
pmc-10570442.description: BackgroundThe changes in the morphology and characteristics of the V1 leads during left bundle branch capturing still need to be fully understood.ObjectiveThis study aims to provide some suggestions about the LBB capture process through the morphology and characteristics of the V1 lead.MethodLBBP using the continuous pacing and morphology monitoring technique during screw-in using a revolving connector (John Jiang's connecting cable).

pmc-11322842.title: Smartwatch Measures of Outdoor Exposure and Myopia in Children
pmc-11322842.creator: Jun Chen, Jingjing Wang, Ziyi Qi, Shang Liu, Lingyi Zhao, Bo Zhang, Kaige Dong, Linlin Du, Jinliuxing Yang, Haidong Zou, Xiangui He, Xun Xu
pmc-11322842.description: Key PointsQuestionAre specific outdoor exposure patterns associated with the development of myopia in children?FindingsThis prospective cohort study involving 2976 children equipped with smartwatches found that outdoor exposure patterns characterized by a continuous period of at least 15 minutes, accompanied by a sunlight intensity of more than 2000 lux, were associated with less myopic shift.

pmc-11391646.title: “Economic exclusion and the health and wellbeing impacts of the oil industry in the Niger Delta region: a qualitative study of Ogoni experiences”
pmc-11391646.creator: Augusta C. Nkem, Susan Devine, Daprim S. Ogaji, Stephanie M. Topp
pmc-11391646.description: BackgroundWhen managed effectively, oil wealth can drive economic development and improve wellbeing. Conversely, as has been the experience in Ogoniland in the Niger Delta, the presence of the oil industry can lead to environmental degradation and social and economic vulnerabilities with negative impacts on health and wellbeing.

pmc-11677520.description: Simple SummaryMalaria is a serious health problem in many tropical and subtropical regions. Anopheles aquasalis mosquitoes are important in malaria research because they help us understand how malaria spreads. These mosquitoes, like other insects, have different needs and behaviors that affect their survival and ability to reproduce.

pmc-12397298.title: Observation of triplet-assisted long-distance charge-transfer exciton transport in single organic cocrystal
pmc-12397298.creator: Yejun Xiao, Xianchang Yan, Rui Cai, Xuan Liu, Jingwen Bao, Min Zhang, Jing Leng, Shengye Jin, Wenming Tian
pmc-12397298.description: Charge-transfer (CT) states with long transport distances are highly desired for promoting the performance of organic optoelectronic devices in photoconversion and electroluminescence. However, due to the limited lifetime and small diffusivity, only nanoscale CT transport has been observed so far.

pmc-12413039.title: The putative AraC-type transcriptional regulator STM1082 facilitates Salmonella pathogenicity through modulation of intestinal invasion and intracellular replication
pmc-12413039.creator: Shuai Ma, Wanwu Li, Xinyue Wang, Yuyang Sun, Houliang Guo, Jiaqi Ma, Lingyan Jiang
pmc-12413039.description: Salmonella is a food-borne zoonotic pathogen that causes human gastroenteritis and potentially fatal systemic infections. The invasion of intestinal epithelial cells and the survival and replication within host macrophages are essential for the intestinal and systemic infections caused by Salmonella, respectively. To precisely regulate the expression of virulence-related genes, Salmonella relies on a series of regulatory proteins.

pmc-13189702.creator: Agnes Yohannan, Archana Gundmi
pmc-13189702.description: IntroductionA ringing sensation in the ear is referred to as tinnitus. It is one of the common symptoms associated with hearing loss. It can be associated even with loudness-related conditions, such as hyperacusis.ObjectiveTo investigate the relationship between tinnitus and hyperacusis in individuals with normal hearing and up-to-mild hearing loss, focusing on the manifestation of loudness intolerance.
